The Birmingham City Sch,ool System accepts its responsibility as specified in Alabama State Board of Education Resolution I-1-f adopted January 11, 1990, for establishing policies and procedures for the Professional Education Personnel Evaluation Program in the schools under its jurisdiction.
All tenure decisions for principals hired on or before June 30, 2000 are subject to the Tenure Act 16-24-1 through 16-24-8.
Principals hired for the first time on or after July 1, 2000 will be subjected to the provisions as outlined in the Teacher Accountability Act. (Alabama Code 16-24B-1 through 16-24B-8)
Leave for performing military service will be granted consistent with, and subject to, the provisions of the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act of 1994, 38 U.S.C. 4301 et.seq., Alabama Code 31-2-13 (as amended), and Alabama Code 31-12-1, et seq.
Sick leave with pay shall be available to all full-time employees in accordance with the State Law as earned at the rate of one day per month for the months employed.

This policy provides basic guidelines for employees regarding the contents of Alabama Code 16-22-9 but does not present the Code in its entirety.
said guidelines and procedures must include those provisions required by law, as found in Alabama Code, 516-22-9 (1975).
References: Ala. Code 16-22-9.
Any reduction in personnel shall procedurally be accomplished in accordance with sees. 16-24-8to -10 Ala. Code (1975).
A determination by the Board that a Reduction in Force (RlF) is necessary pursuant to this policy constitutes the necessary cause for dismissal required by § 36-26-1 02~ Ala. Code (1975).
Any reduction in personnel shall procedurally be accomplished in accordance with § 36-26-100 to -108, Ala. Code (1975).
Nothing in this policy shall be deemed to create a property interest in continued employment, or to create an expectation of further or continued employment beyond that provided by, whether applicable, the Alabama Fair Dismissal Act, § 36-26-100, et. seq., Ala. Code (1975).
"Employee" as used in this policy is defined in the exact manner as that term is defined in § 36-26-100, Ala. Code (1975) and as construed by applicable law.
"Probationary employee" is defined as that term is defined by § 36-26-101, Ala. Code (1975) and as construed by applicable case law.
Termination of probationary employee pursuant to § 36-26-101(c), Ala. Code (1975) is not a "reduction in force" as used in this policy.
Nothing in this policy shall affect the rights of the employing Board to remove a probationary employee as contemplated by § 36-26-100(c), Ala. Code (1975), or create procedural requirements for such removal beyond those set out in § 36-26-101(c), Ala. Code (1975).
It is the goal of the Birmingham City Board of Education ("the School Board") to provide and promote a policy that ensures adequate and sufficient process for employees proposed for discipline under both the Alabama Fair Dismissal Act, Code of Alabama §§ 36-26-100, et seq., and the Teacher Tenure Act, Code of Alabama §§ 16-24-1 et seq., as well as the necessary expeditious resolution of employment conflicts.

Employees who are not exempt from the provisions of the Fair Labor Standard Act shall be scheduled for overtime work only with the prior approval of the employee's direct supervisor and the Superintendent.
Employees who work overtime shall have a choice between being compensated pursuant to the provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act, or being granted compensatory time pursuant to the provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act.
